own_solution.law: Hydrostatic pressure: P = P_surface + rho g h
assumptions: pressure at free surface stays 101 kPa

defect_reasons.other: T1799 (and T4031) raise the surface pressure while the problem states the free-surface pressure is 101 kPa; T4031 says 'then', but T1799 has no temporal marker, so a reader may see tension with the stated 101 kPa; T8558/TECE9 leave implicit that the question refers to the time after the rise is released.

notes: Base answer 101000 + 1000*9.8*12 = 218600 Pa = 218.6 kPa. With a sustained 15 kPa rise: 233.6 kPa. The transient pump sentences (T8558, TECE9) produce a rise that is removed, so the net effect on the final state is zero; I classed them C (belongs to the system, appears in the surface-pressure relation, net contribution cancels). Base area sentences (T2A78, T9E55): area enters a force balance on a liquid column and cancels from the pressure, so C. Variant check: T8558, T4031, T5D28, T1799 all state 15 kPa; TECE9 and TB26D state 'a small pressure rise' with no number, so if they are meant as variants of the 15 kPa sentences they differ in the number (deliberate non-numeric versions presumably). T2A78 and T9E55 both 2 m^2.
